speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me when the wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions started, and if they appeared suddenly or gradually?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your recent trip to Minnesota and the pattern of migratory joint pain, have you noticed any expanding red rash on your skin or had any known tick bites while camping? I need to rule out Lyme disease, so REQUEST TEST: Lyme serology and REQUEST IMAGES of the skin lesions.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the Lyme serology is negative, I need to explore other causes for your migratory arthritis and skin lesions. Have you experienced any recent sore throat, joint swelling in other areas, or a history of rheumatic fever?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of fever, migratory arthritis, and those specific violaceous vesiculopustular lesions strongly suggests Meningococcemia. REQUEST TEST: Blood culture and REQUEST IMAGES of the skin lesions.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Blood Culture: Pending at the time of examination; Skin Imaging: Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions noted on the dorsum of both wrists and hands; two lesions on the left palm.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have a history of recurrent joint pain or other autoimmune conditions? Given the classic presentation of fever, migratory arthritis, and characteristic lesions, I am proceeding with treatment for meningococcemia while awaiting culture results. DIAGNOSIS READY: Meningococcemia
